content.title: Detroit Pistons vs Orlando Magic Live Stream: How to Watch NBA
content.text: The Orlando Magic host the Detroit Pistons, looking for their third win in a row and a chance to tie this season series on Monday. The Detroit Pistons go for their fourth win in a row and the season series win against the Orlando Magic on Monday night. The Magic are going for their third win in a row, but this game is more important for Orlando. The Pistons have already clinched the top seed in the Eastern Conference for the first time since 2007. Orlando has clinched a play-in position, but the Magic are trying to improve their standing, currently sitting in ninth in the East. There is still a lot of opportunity left for Orlando as it is just a half-game back of the eighth-place Charlotte Hornets. The Pistons lead this series 2-1, after beating the Magic 1-6-92 on March 1. Cade Cunningham led the charge for Detroit in that matchup with a game-high 29 points and 11 assists, while Tobias Harris added 23 points to help lead the Pistons to their sixth straight road victory at the time. Cunningham won’t be available for this series finale, as he is still recovering from a collapsed lung. The Pistons’ superstar is expected to return on April 10. Regardless, Detroit is still the 3.5-point favorite to win this series tonight. Detroit is coming off a comfortable 116-93 over the Philadelphia 76ers on the road on Saturday for its third straight win. The Pistons swept the season series against Philly, 4-0. Harris took charge in the absence of Cunningham with a team-high 19 points, and Daniss Jenkins added 16 points with 14 assists. The game clinched the Pistons’ spot as the conference’s top seed for the first time in nearly two decades. The Pistons took advantage of the Sixers’ absence of Joel Embiid, leading by 10 in the first quarter, and went on a 15-4 run to end the first half. That snowballed into a 26-point lead in the second half in a game that wasn’t really close against the sixth-seeded Sixers. This team is truly the class in the East, just two years removed from winning 14 games. Orlando is coming off a close 112-108 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Sunday. Desmond Bane led the Magic with 27 points and overcame a 15-point deficit in the second half to sweep the series 2-0 over New Orleans. The Magic were also able to overcome a game-high 32 points from Saddiq Bey. It will be difficult to play on back-to-back nights for Orlando, let alone play the best team in the conference.
